...obviously.

Noon interrupts me.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese marks the work being interrupted by or spanning the lunch break. The English personifies noon as directly interrupting the narrator and does not convey the break in activity.

rows.jp: ……なんか、想像していた部活と違う。
rows.en: ...Not quite the club activity I had imagined.

I had forgotten,

rows.en: That humanity had long since vanished.

ghs.en: how long ago mankind had gone.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says the narrator had forgotten the fact that humanity vanished long ago. The English says he forgot how long ago it happened, preserving awareness of the event but losing track only of its timing.
ghs.remedy: that humanity had vanished long ago.

highlights.text: how long ago mankind had gone.

rows.jp: 俺たち八人だけの世界。いや、もう七人だ。
rows.en: A world with only eight of us. No, seven now.

ghs.en: This is a world of just us eight. No, now it's us seven.

rows.en: We were a flame guttering in the wind.

ghs.en: We are as a candle in front of the wind.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese idiom depicts a flame about to be blown out, meaning their continued existence is in imminent peril. The literal English image is not an established equivalent and leaves that implication opaque.
ghs.remedy: We're a candle flame about to be snuffed out.

highlights.text: We are as a candle in front of the wind.

rows.jp: カップラーメンにお湯をそそぐ。

and eat.

rows.jp: 「おはようございます。遅かったですね」

Misato: "Yes..."
Feeling down,

ghs.en: and glasses clouded over as well.

rows.jp: 「ショッキングな出来事がありましたね」

Misato: "Yes, very."

rows.jp: 俺の近くにぺたりと座って、ぼんやりと空を見あげる。

rows.en: “...You'll feel better if you talk about it.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...talk, and happiness will come back."

ghs.en: Misato: "I have been... fighting with Tomoki."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese reports that she got into a fight with Tomoki, a completed incident that explains her present mood. The English progressive presents an ongoing series or action instead.
ghs.remedy: I... had a fight with Tomoki.

highlights.text: I have been... fighting with Tomoki.

rows.jp: 「はあ、友貴とですか。俺もよくしますよ」
rows.en: “Oh. With Tomoki? We do that all the time.”

rows.jp: 先輩は疲れたように微笑む。

ghs.en: Senpai smiled as if looking very tired.

rows.jp: 「ああいう喧嘩とは、また違う喧嘩ですよ」
rows.en: “This was a different kind of fight.”

ghs.en: Misato: "That sort of fight is quite different from this kind of fight."

rows.jp: 「複雑な家庭事情ってやつですか。食べます？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "This is about complicated household circumstances, then. Will you eat?"

rows.jp: 先輩は弱々しく首を振る。

ghs.en: Senpai gives me a weak shake of the head.

rows.jp: 「……二人っきりの姉弟なんですけど……どうにもうまくいきません」
rows.en: “...It's only the two of us, sister and brother... but we still can't seem to get along.”

ghs.en: Misato: "...we are siblings, the only two, and yet... there is nothing that we can do to make this work well."

rows.jp: 「友貴もあれで強情ですからね」
rows.en: “Tomoki may not look it, but he can be stubborn.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Because Tomoki has also some obstinacy himself."

rows.jp: 「……原因はわたしにあるんです」

ghs.en: Misato: "...the fault for this resides all with me."

rows.en: In silence, I prompted her to continue.

ghs.en: Wordlessly I urge her on.

rows.jp: 「わたし、口うるさいですから」

ghs.en: Misato: "Because I... am a shrew."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese self-criticism is that she nags or fusses too much. 'Shrew' is a much harsher gendered character judgment and changes the restrained self-reproach into an insult.
ghs.remedy: Because I... nag him too much.

ghs.en: Taichi: "You are, now?"
Misato: "...I am the one at fault!"

rows.jp: 自嘲して、前髪をいじった。

ghs.en: She ridiculed herself and played with her bangs.
Taichi: "Theeen, you are just like me!"
Misato: "...is that how I am?"
ghs.assessment: After the narrator says he is like her, the Japanese asks whether that is really true about him. The English instead has her ask for confirmation about her own nature.

rows.jp: 「俺もすごく悪いんで。だからここにいるんですけど」
rows.en: “I'm pretty bad myself. That's why I'm here.”

Taichi: "If it is together with you, Senpai!"

ghs.remedy: Senpai's face blossoms into a little girl's smile.

highlights.text: Senpai's smile frays around the edges like little girl's.

rows.jp: 「いーですねー、わるいことー」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Awesooome, yes, something baaad."

Kiri: "You are in danger, quickly!"

rows.en: “Getting all worked up again. What's wrong?”

Taichi: "?!"
Touko?

rows.en: “I went to see her, and she was dead... You killed her!”

ghs.en: Kiri: "We went to see her, and she was dead... and you killed her!"

rows.en: “I said I don't know! Are you serious? Was Touko really dead?”

ghs.assessment: The Japanese identifies Kirihara-senpai's house. The English substitutes Hasekura, changing the named location and person associated with it.

rows.jp: 「胸を刃物でひとつきにされて……」

ghs.en: Kiri: "Her chest was pierced through with a bladed weapon..."

One miss and it's all done.

rows.en: Overpowering Kiri would be easy, but—

Kiri: "...ah!"
The bolt fired.

Kiri: "But!"

Miki: "Ah, soHrry."
Kiri: "Stay back!"

Taichi: "I won't do anything!"

rows.en: “...Though I'd love to knock you across the roof.”

highlights.text: I'd like to toss you off somewhere

Kiri falls on her backside.

rows.en: “Murderer! Who are you going to kill next!?”

ghs.en: Kiri: "Murderer! Who are you going to kill next?!"

ghs.en: Taichi: "...really, you, Kiri... your bad parts are showing. The point is, I just barely now learned that Touko's dead. How does it automatically become something I have done!"

Taichi: "...first would be the one who found her, which would be you."

highlights.text: Just make the world happy and die!

inviting disappointed dejection.
